Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall contain all relevant data or details of the means used by the manufacturer to ensure that the product and manufacturer processes comply with Annex I, and shall at least contain Annex VII elements.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a technical-file-style evidence package showing how the product and vulnerability-handling processes meet the preliminary and final CRA requirement registers.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as voluntary technical-file readiness; formal obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: The current project does not perform CE marking, but a technical documentation package is the organizing evidence artifact for voluntary CRA readiness and later control/evidence mapping.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment determines final applicability, implementation depth, and which evidence is necessary for each Annex I requirement.
Required security capability: Technical file structure; evidence index; requirement-to-evidence traceability; document ownership and versioning.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.1 Technical File; §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment; §3.4 Secure Development Properties
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: technical file index; requirement registers; control/evidence matrix; architecture docs; SBOM; security test reports.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall be drawn up before market placement and continuously updated where appropriate, at least during the support period.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should create the technical-file-style package before any voluntary certification claim or release-readiness assertion, and update it for major releases, risk-assessment changes, vulnerability-handling changes, support-period changes, and significant architecture changes.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as voluntary readiness; formal timing obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: For readiness work, the technical file must be built before final control sign-off, not after the fact. TokenStream changes through services, policies, providers, MCP, ingestion, dependencies, and containers.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define update triggers and review cadence.
Required security capability: Technical documentation lifecycle; change-triggered updates; support-period documentation maintenance; release evidence retention.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.4 Sustainability & Review; §7.1 Technical File; §6.1 Support Period
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: document version history; release checklist; update trigger list; technical file custodian.

Normative requirement: For products also subject to other Union legal acts requiring technical documentation, draw up a single set of technical documentation containing Annex VII information and information required by those acts.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should record whether any other Union legal acts requiring technical documentation are in scope; if future scope changes, the CRA technical file should be integrated rather than duplicated.
Preliminary applicability: Not applicable in current stated scope unless other legal-act scope is identified
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream is being assessed as open-source, non-commercial software readiness. No other Union technical-documentation act has been identified for the current scope.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment may identify AI/data/security contexts, but legal analysis determines whether another Union technical-documentation regime applies.
Required security capability: Cross-framework scope review; single technical file strategy; legal trigger tracking.
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: legal scope memo; cross-framework applicability assessment; single-file index if future scope changes.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation and conformity-assessment correspondence shall be drawn up in an official language of the notified body's Member State or a language acceptable to that body.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should keep current voluntary certification/readiness documents in English; if a notified body is used in future, confirm accepted language before formal submission.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as language-readiness note; formal notified-body obligation conditional on conformity procedure
Preliminary applicability rationale: There is no notified body in the current no-CE scope, but the user has decided that certification documents are in English.
Risk assessment dependency: This is not driven by cybersecurity risk; it is driven by conformity-assessment route and notified-body acceptance.
Required security capability: Documentation language policy; formal submission language trigger.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.1 Technical File; §7.4 EU DoC & CE Marking
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: documentation language decision; future notified-body language confirmation if applicable.

Normative requirement: Commission may add elements to Annex VII technical documentation by delegated acts to account for technological and implementation developments, with proportionate burden for microenterprises and SMEs.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should monitor delegated acts and update the technical-file template when Annex VII content expectations change.
Preliminary applicability rationale: Technical documentation content may evolve. A static template could become stale before future formal scope or certification claim.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment may indicate which evidence is security-relevant, but delegated acts determine added formal content.
Required security capability: Regulatory monitoring; technical file template maintenance; delegated-act change review.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.7 Harmonized Standards Tracking; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: regulatory watch log; technical-file template version history; change-impact notes.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall contain at least the listed information, as applicable to the relevant product.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should treat Annex VII as the minimum evidence table of contents, with explicit applicability decisions for software-only, OSS, self-hosted deployment, no-CE current scope, and optional services.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as voluntary technical-file table of contents
Preliminary applicability rationale: The phrase "as applicable" requires product-context decisions. TokenStream has software-only elements, optional services, and no hardware marking/photos.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment and legal scope determine what is applicable and how much detail is required.
Required security capability: Annex VII table of contents; applicability marking; evidence completeness review.
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: Annex VII checklist; applicability rationale register; evidence owner list.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include a general product description including intended purpose.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should document that it is an open-source AI orchestration and retrieval runtime for self-hosted deployments behind client applications, including intended workflows and non-goals.
Preliminary applicability rationale: Intended purpose anchors risk assessment, foreseeable use, user instructions, and Annex I applicability.
Risk assessment dependency: TokenStream risk assessment should use this intended purpose as the baseline for threat scenarios and misuse analysis.
Required security capability: Product description; intended use; non-goals; deployment model definition.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.5 Product Assessment; §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: README; overview docs; product scope statement; architecture summary.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include versions of software affecting compliance with essential cybersecurity requirements.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should identify versions that affect cybersecurity compliance, including product version, Git commit/tag, service image tags/digests, Python/npm dependency lockfiles, base images, Qdrant/MinIO/TEI/Open WebUI versions, and configuration schema versions.
Preliminary applicability rationale: Version traceability is required for vulnerability handling, advisories, SBOMs, reproducing evidence, and determining affected deployments.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should identify which software components are security-relevant and must be version-tracked.
Required security capability: Version inventory; release traceability; dependency and image version tracking; configuration versioning.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.1 SBOM Generation; §3.3 Provenance & Integrity; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: version.txt; Git tags; image digests; SBOM; lockfiles; release manifest.

Normative requirement: For hardware products, technical documentation shall include photographs or illustrations showing external features, marking, and internal layout.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should record this as not applicable because the assessed product is software-only; architecture diagrams may still be included under Annex VII (2)(a).
Preliminary applicability: Not applicable in current software-only TokenStream scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream has no physical hardware product, packaging, physical marking, or internal hardware layout.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment does not make this applicable unless product scope changes to hardware or embedded distribution.
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: software-only scope statement; N/A rationale.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include user information and instructions as set out in Annex II.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should include or reference secure installation, configuration, operation, update, support-period, vulnerability reporting, data deletion, and integrator instructions.
Preliminary applicability rationale: Self-hosted security depends heavily on operator choices such as exposed ports, secrets, provider credentials, MCP tools, uploads, and reverse proxy/TLS configuration.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should identify security-critical operator instructions and foreseeable misuse.
Required security capability: Secure user documentation; Annex II mapping; operator hardening guidance; integrator guidance.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.3 User-Facing Documentation; §7.2 Downstream Customer Provisioning
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: README; quickstart; operate guide; security configuration guide; Annex II checklist.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall describe design and development, including drawings/schemes and system architecture explaining how software components build on or feed into each other and integrate into overall processing.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should document service architecture, trust boundaries, data flows, API boundaries, runtime snapshots, corpus ingestion lifecycle, retrieval lifecycle, provider/tool integration, and storage/index topology.
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream is multi-service and configuration-driven. Architecture evidence is needed to justify controls for access, confidentiality, integrity, availability, attack surface, and vulnerability handling.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should be based on these diagrams and update them when architecture changes.
Required security capability: Architecture documentation; data-flow diagrams; component dependency diagrams; trust-boundary mapping.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.4.9 Threat Model; §7.1 Technical File; §3.4 Secure Development Properties
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: services overview; Mermaid diagrams; API contracts; docker-compose topology; data-flow diagram.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall describe vulnerability handling processes, including SBOM, CVD policy, evidence of contact address for reporting vulnerabilities, and technical solutions for secure update distribution.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a vulnerability-handling package containing SBOM process, vulnerability intake, CVD policy, security contact, triage/remediation workflow, advisory process, and secure update distribution approach for source and container releases.
Preliminary applicability rationale: This is the technical-file evidence counterpart of Annex I Part II and Article 14 readiness. TokenStream already has SECURITY.md but needs fuller process evidence.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define vulnerability scope, severity criteria, update channels, and reporting thresholds.
Required security capability: Vulnerability handling documentation; SBOM; CVD policy; security contact; secure update distribution; advisory workflow.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.1-§3.2 SBOM; §4.1-§4.4 Vulnerability Handling; §6.1 Secure Updates
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: SBOM; SECURITY.md; CVD policy; advisory template; release/update guide; contact proof.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include information/specifications of production and monitoring processes and validation of those processes.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should document release/build processes, CI checks, dependency/container scanning, security test gates, SBOM generation, image publishing, vulnerability monitoring, evidence retention, and validation of those processes.
Preliminary applicability rationale: For software, "production" maps to build, release, packaging, image publishing, and release monitoring. These processes determine whether evidence is repeatable and trustworthy.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define which process failures create cybersecurity risk and which validations are required.
Required security capability: Secure build/release process; monitoring process; CI validation; release evidence retention; process validation.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.3 Provenance & Integrity; §3.4 Security Testing; §4.1 Vulnerability Monitoring; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: CI workflow; scan reports; release checklist; SBOM generation logs; image publishing evidence.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include the cybersecurity risk assessment under Article 13, including how Annex I Part I requirements are applicable.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should include the product risk assessment and final Annex I Part I applicability rationale in the technical-file package.
Preliminary applicability rationale: This is the strongest confirmation that risk assessment follows preliminary requirement analysis and finalizes applicability.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment is the required source for final applicability and implementation rationale.
Required security capability: Cybersecurity risk assessment; final applicability register; risk-to-requirement traceability.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment; §7.1.1-§7.1.2 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: risk assessment report; final Annex I Part I register; risk treatment plan; threat model.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include relevant information used to determine the support period under Article 13(8).
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should include the support-period or rolling-release support model rationale, expected use assumptions, supported versions/images, dependency support constraints, and end-of-support communication approach.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness scope; formal support-period obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream users need to know how long security updates and advisories apply. The rationale is needed if the project uses latest-only or rolling support.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform expected use time, deployment assumptions, and dependency support constraints.
Required security capability: Support-period rationale; version support model; EoS communication; lifecycle evidence.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §6.1 Support Period & Update Obligations; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: support policy; support-period rationale memo; supported-version matrix; EoS template.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include a list of harmonised standards applied in full or in part whose references have been published in the Official Journal.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a standards/applicability register. Until harmonised CRA standards are selected or available, the register should identify "none applied" or "pending", plus non-normative references such as OpenChain used only for implementation/evidence cross-check.
Preliminary applicability rationale: Standards claims create conformity implications. TokenStream must distinguish normative harmonised standards from OpenChain guidance and other good-practice frameworks.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment may indicate standards usefulness, but standards applicability depends on legal/conformity strategy.
Required security capability: Standards tracking; harmonised-standard applicability; non-normative guidance separation.
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: standards watch log; standards applicability register; OpenChain cross-reference notes.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include reports of tests carried out to verify conformity of the product and vulnerability-handling processes with applicable Annex I Part I and Part II requirements.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should retain security test reports and process validation evidence for application code, APIs, auth/RBAC, ingestion/parsers, dependencies, containers, frontend/admin flows, update distribution, and vulnerability handling.
Preliminary applicability rationale: Testing evidence is needed to support claims about secure defaults, access control, attack surface, vulnerability handling, and release readiness.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define test scope, frequency, and depth.
Required security capability: Security test evidence; process validation; release gate; vulnerability-handling validation.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.4.5-§3.4.10 Security Testing; §4 Vulnerability Handling; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: SAST reports; dependency/container scans; DAST/API tests; threat-model review; tabletop exercise; release gate results.

Normative requirement: Technical documentation shall include a copy of the EU declaration of conformity.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should mark this as not applicable in the current no-CE/non-commercial OSS scope; if formal market placement occurs later, the DoC copy belongs in the technical file.
Preliminary applicability: Not applicable to current non-commercial OSS objective; legal-scope trigger only
Preliminary applicability rationale: The user has explicitly stated there will be no actual CE marking. Including this row sets a clean boundary between readiness documentation and formal conformity artifacts.
Risk assessment dependency: Legal scope and conformity assessment outcome determine applicability, not cybersecurity risk alone.
Required security capability: DoC trigger management; no-DoC disclaimer; future technical-file slot.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.3 EU DoC & CE Marking; §7.4 EU Declaration of Conformity & CE Marking
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates if future scope changes: EU DoC; simplified DoC URL; DoC version history.

Normative requirement: Where applicable, technical documentation shall include the SBOM upon reasoned request from a market surveillance authority where necessary to check Annex I compliance.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain release-specific SBOMs that can be provided in a future formal scope; in current voluntary readiness, SBOMs should be generated and retained as evidence, without implying an active MSA obligation.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as SBOM readiness; formal MSA request obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream's dependency-heavy architecture makes SBOM useful for vulnerability management and evidence even outside formal authority requests.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define SBOM scope, depth, optional-service inclusion, and sensitivity concerns.
Required security capability: SBOM generation; SBOM retention; release-to-SBOM mapping; authority/customer disclosure decision.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.1 SBOM Generation; §3.2 SBOM Data Quality; §7.1.4 SBOM in Technical File; §7.2 SBOM Provisioning
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM; SBOM validation report; release manifest; SBOM archive.
